summary: This component renders a blog post item that adapts based on whether you're viewing a single post or browsing a list. When viewing the full post, it shows additional elements like related posts, social sharing, and reader engagement tools. The component imports specialized sub-components to handle different sections of the post layout.

explanations.23: This helper hook checks if we're on the actual blog post page versus a list view, then returns a CSS class name to add bottom spacing only in list view where multiple posts appear together.
explanations.24: The useBlogPost hook gives us context about whether we're viewing a full post page or just seeing a preview card in a list.
explanations.25: The conditional returns a margin class name if we're NOT on the blog post page, otherwise returns undefined which means no extra margin is added.
explanations.29: We're extracting metadata about the current post and a flag indicating if the reader is on the full post page or just browsing a list.
explanations.34: The ArticleActions component (buttons, sharing options, etc.) only displays on the full post page itself—not when the post appears as a card in a blog list.
explanations.46: The TranslationNotice banner only shows on the full post page, before the main content, so translators can't accidentally modify it and it doesn't clutter the post list.
explanations.51: This entire block of engagement components—Bluesky, related posts, typo reporting, reactions—only renders when someone is reading the full post, not when browsing the blog list.
explanations.64: This TriedIt component renders unless the front matter explicitly sets tried_it to false, giving you the ability to hide it on specific posts.
